readmeExcerpt: _Official golang implementation of the Canopy Network Protocol_ # Overview ### ⫸ **Welcome to the Network that Powers the Peer-to-Peer Launchpad for New Chains** Built on a recursive architecture, chains bootstrap each other into independence — forming an `unstoppable` web of utility and security. **Here you'll find:** ➪ A recursive framework to build blockchains. ➪ The seed chain that started the recursive cycle. For more information on the Canopy Network Protocol visit [https://canopynetwork.org](https://canopynetwork.org) ## Standard ➪ Canopy is an Ethereum-RPC compatible L1 for native transfers, so it can plug into existing Ethereum exchange, wallet, and indexer tooling, including MetaMask. Use the `/v1/eth` endpoint as a custom Ethereum RPC and review the compatibility notes in the [eth-spec](./fsm/ethereum.md) ## RPC ➪ [Full RPC Specification](./cmd/rpc/README.md) ## Protocol Documentation ➪ Check out the Canopy Network wiki: [https://canopy-network.gitbook.io/docs](https://canopy-network.gitbook.io/docs) ## Repository Documentation Welcome to the Canopy Network reference implementation. This repository can be well understood reading about the core modules: - [Controller](controller/README.md): Coordinates communication between all the major parts of the Canopy blockchain, like a central hub or "bus" that connects the system together. - [Finite State Machine (FSM)](fsm/README.md): Defines the logic for how transactions change the blockchain's state — it decides what’s valid and how state transitions happen from one block to the next. - [Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) Consensus](bft/README.md): A consensus mechanism that allows the network to agree on new blocks even if some nodes are unreliable or malicious. - [Peer-to-Peer Networking](p2p/README.md): A secure and encrypted communication system that lets nodes talk directly to each other without needing a central server. - [Persistence](store/README.md): Manages the blockchain’s storage — it saves the current state (ledger), indexes past transactions, and ensures fast and reliable data verification. ## How to Run It ➪ To run the Canopy binary, use the following commands: ```bash make build/canopy-full canopy start ``` ## How to Run It with 🐳 Docker ➪ To run a Canopy `Localnet` in a *containerized* environment, use the following commands: ```bash make docker/build make docker/up-fast make docker/logs or simply make docker/up && make docker/logs ``` ## Running Tests ➪ To run Canopy unit tests, use the Go testing tools: ```bash make test ``` ## How to Contribute ➪ Canopy is an open-source project, and we welcome contributions from the community. Here's how to get involved: 1. **Fork** the repository and clone it locally. 2. **Code** your improvements or fixes. 3. **Submit a Pull Request** (PR) for review. ➣ Please follow these [guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) to maintain high-quality contributions: ### High Impact or Architectural Changes ➪ Before making large changes, discuss them with the Canopy team on [Discord](https://discord.gg/pNcSJj7Wdh) to ensure alignment. ### Coding Style - Code must adhere to official Go formatting (use [`gofmt`](https://golang.org/cmd/gofmt)). - (Optional) Use [EditorConfig](https://editorconfig.org) for consistent formatting. - All code should follow Go documentation/commentary guidelines. - PRs should be opened against the `development` branch. ## Contact
readmeHtml:
Official golang implementation of the Canopy Network Protocol

Overview

⫸ Welcome to the Network that Powers the Peer-to-Peer Launchpad for New Chains

Built on a recursive architecture, chains bootstrap each other into independence —
forming an unstoppable web of utility and security.

Here you'll find:

➪ A recursive framework to build blockchains.

➪ The seed chain that started the recursive cycle.

For more information on the Canopy Network Protocol visit https://canopynetwork.org

Standard

➪ Canopy is an Ethereum-RPC compatible L1 for native transfers, so it can plug into existing Ethereum exchange, wallet, and indexer tooling, including MetaMask. Use the /v1/eth endpoint as a custom Ethereum RPC and review the compatibility notes in the eth-spec

RPC

➪ Full RPC Specification

Protocol Documentation

➪ Check out the Canopy Network wiki: https://canopy-network.gitbook.io/docs

Repository Documentation

Welcome to the Canopy Network reference implementation. This repository can be well understood reading about the core modules:

  • Controller: Coordinates communication between all the major parts of the Canopy blockchain, like a central hub or "bus" that connects the system together.
  • Finite State Machine (FSM): Defines the logic for how transactions change the blockchain's state — it decides what’s valid and how state transitions happen from one block to the next.
  • Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) Consensus: A consensus mechanism that allows the network to agree on new blocks even if some nodes are unreliable or malicious.
  • Peer-to-Peer Networking: A secure and encrypted communication system that lets nodes talk directly to each other without needing a central server.
  • Persistence: Manages the blockchain’s storage — it saves the current state (ledger), indexes past transactions, and ensures fast and reliable data verification.

How to Run It

➪ To run the Canopy binary, use the following commands:

make build/canopy-full
canopy start

How to Run It with 🐳 Docker

➪ To run a Canopy Localnet in a containerized environment, use the following commands:

make docker/build
make docker/up-fast
make docker/logs

or simply

make docker/up && make docker/logs

Running Tests

➪ To run Canopy unit tests, use the Go testing tools:

make test

How to Contribute

➪ Canopy is an open-source project, and we welcome contributions from the community. Here's how to get involved:

  1. Fork the repository and clone it locally.
  2. Code your improvements or fixes.
  3. Submit a Pull Request (PR) for review.

➣ Please follow these guidelines to maintain high-quality contributions:

High Impact or Architectural Changes

➪ Before making large changes, discuss them with the Canopy team on Discord to ensure alignment.

Coding Style

  • Code must adhere to official Go formatting (use gofmt).
  • (Optional) Use EditorConfig for consistent formatting.
  • All code should follow Go documentation/commentary guidelines.
  • PRs should be opened against the development branch.

Contact

aiSummary.oneLiner: A decentralized network protocol designed to provide secure, censorship-resistant access to information.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Canopy is a peer-to-peer network infrastructure project aimed at bypassing traditional internet censorship and surveillance. It utilizes a custom routing protocol that obscures traffic patterns, making it difficult for ISPs or state actors to identify or block connections. The system relies on a distributed network of nodes to serve content securely, ensuring that there is no single point of failure or centralized authority that can be targeted. It is built to support the deployment of decentralized applications and resilient information sharing in restrictive environments.
keyFeatures: Obfuscated routing protocol: Hides traffic patterns and metadata to prevent deep packet inspection and censorship.
Decentralized node architecture: Distributes network load and content across peers, removing central points of failure.
Cryptographic identity management: Uses public-key cryptography to ensure secure, verifiable communication between nodes.
Resilient content distribution: Ensures information remains accessible even if large portions of the network are offline or blocked.
Low-bandwidth optimization: Designed to function effectively in regions with poor connectivity or restricted internet access.

useCases.title: Censorship circumvention
useCases.description: Activists and journalists use the network to access and share information securely in countries with strict internet controls.

useCases.title: Decentralized application hosting
useCases.description: Developers build resilient dApps on top of the protocol that cannot be taken down by traditional hosting providers.

useCases.title: Secure communication
useCases.description: Whistleblowers utilize the obfuscated routing to communicate with journalists without revealing their location or identity.

useCases.title: Resilient infrastructure research
useCases.description: Academics study the protocol to understand how decentralized networks can survive targeted attacks and disruptions.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Privacy advocates, activists, and developers building decentralized systems. Requires technical knowledge to run a node or build applications on the network.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Download the client, generate your cryptographic identity, and connect to an existing bootstrap node.
